learning_level.placement: The four scores 4/5/4/5 sum to 18; their arithmetic mean is 4.50 and rounds half-up to Level 5. The published result is Level 5.

quality.source_quality: Config-entry states, locks, immutable mappings, retry handles, failure reasons, runtime data, and unload callbacks are explicit and strongly typed throughout the lifecycle.
quality.architecture: The entry and manager coordinate with the integration loader, component setup, core jobs and events, dispatcher, and storage through recognizable boundaries.
quality.naming_and_idiom: ConfigEntry, ConfigEntries, async_setup, async_migrate, ConfigEntryNotReady, runtime_data, unload, reload, and state names expose lifecycle intent.
quality.tests: Focused core and config-entry tests cover setup races, locks, invalid transitions, migration, exponential backoff, authentication failures, concurrent reload, unload, persistence, thread ownership, and shutdown.
quality.documentation: Developer architecture and integration guidance explain configuration entries, setup, migration, availability failures, unloading, and concurrency rules needed for the path.
quality.traceability: A persisted entry can be followed from manager lookup and locking through loading, migration, component setup, retries and state events into successful load, reload, unload, storage updates, and shutdown cancellation.
quality.maintainability: Typed states, per-entry synchronization, loader and setup boundaries, explicit retry ownership, and focused lifecycle tests constrain changes in this high-concurrency path.
quality.educational_value: The selected slice teaches expert asynchronous plugin lifecycle design without requiring knowledge of any particular device protocol or the entire Home Assistant platform.
